newsitem.title: MALTA: Libya "jittery" over warships visiting Malta.
newsitem.headline: Libya "jittery" over warships visiting Malta.

text.p: Libyan Foreign Minister Omar Mustafa al-Montasser said on Friday Libya felt "jittery" when foreign warships visited Malta.
Speaking at a news conference with Maltese Foreign Minister George Vella, Montasser said: "We do not like it, they are too close, but we understand Malta's position."

"These visits create some activity in Malta, and we appreciate that the Maltese dockyard is not open to foreign warships, but when the enemy, like the United States, gets too close, one gets jittery," Montasser said.

Two U.S. ships, the guided missile cruiser Vella Gulf and the amphibious assault ship Nassau, have visited Malta since the Labour government took office in October. But in March the government announced the number of foreign warships visiting Malta would be restricted.
Montasser regretted Libya has not been invited to the second Euro-Med foreign ministers' meeting, due to be attended by EU and Mediterranean Arab foreign ministers in Malta on April 15 and 16.
"We cannot understand how Libya, which has one of the longest coastlines of the Mediterranean, has been excluded. It makes us a little uncomfortable," Montasser said.

Montasser and Vella said they had discussed various bilateral matters, including the possibility of a Libya-Italy gas pipeline passing through Maltese waters and the possibility, still in its very early stages, of a Libyan bank opening in Malta.
Montasser said problems on overdue payments for Maltese exports to Libya had been caused by bureaucracy but this was being sorted out.
Vella reiterated Malta's position that it will continue to respect UN sanctions against Libya, although the country felt the decision should be reviewed.
Montasser also met Maltese Prime Minister Alfred Sant in the first high-level meeting between the two countries since the Labour government took office.
